newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia in huge search to find storm missing.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia in huge search to find storm missing.

text.p: A massive search and rescue operation has been launched to find more than 100 people still missing after a Christmas day storm killed at least 106 in eastern Malaysia, officials said on Friday.

They said nearly 300 rescue workers have been deployed and more were expected to join the operation on Friday at the worst affected area, the logging town of Keningau in Malaysia's Sabah state on Borneo island.

The operation involved the armed forces, the Royal Malaysian Air Force, airline Sabah Air, government staff and local residents, officer in-charge of Keningau district, Louis Rampas, told Bernama news agency.
Rampas said 500 houses in nine villages along the Pampang, Bayayo, Liawan and Sinagang rivers were washed away, leaving about 3,000 people homeless.
The New Straits Times daily said 91 of the 102 bodies found in Keningau, 150 km (95 miles) south of Sabah's capital Kota Kinabalu, had been claimed by relatives by Thursday night.
A majority of the dead were Filipino and Indonesian migrant workers living in accommodation built for them along the four rivers in Keningau by sawmill owners, it said.
"There are bodies everywhere," Rampas was quoted as saying. Most of the bodies were found among fallen branches, along the riverbanks and trapped in the debris of their homes, he said.
Sabah Police Commissioner Maizan Shaari said on Thursday night the death toll could rise further.

Officials said tropical storm Greg, which blew ashore in Sabah from the South China Sea at 70 kph (44 mph), snapped power lines and broke road and communication links to Keningau, which is hidden under thick forest cover and nestled between mountains.
The Maritime Rescue and Coordination Centre in Malaysia said several ships were driven to shallow waters in the South China Sea by the storm. No details of the rescue were available.
Sabah is a popular holiday destination but officials said Keningau, a logging town of 60,000, was not a regular tourist spot. They said "initial findings" showed no foreign tourists among the dead.
It was one of the worst storms to hit Sabah in living memory.
There was no immediate estimate of damage to crops. Sabah is a major grower of cocoa but Keningau only supplies a small portion of the crop, growers said.
